audience: Engineers new to the proposal-versus-verification distinction.
prerequisites: Autoregressive generation appends tokens from a committed prefix.
objective: Distinguish block-parallel proposals and one all-accepted batched target verification from three serial target calls, without mistaking call-count reduction for guaranteed lower latency.
scope: All eight narration blocks of the explicitly block-parallel model/token flow illustration. It is not a scaled latency diagram, rejection algorithm, or full DFlash architecture.
assumptions: The displayed continuation is can, reason, fast and all candidates are accepted.
One block-drafting pass predicts the three proposals in parallel; standard autoregressive drafting would be sequential.
Target-call counters count target calls only, not drafting work.
No algorithm timing is measured or drawn to scale here. The closing narration explicitly distinguishes target-call reduction from guaranteed latency reduction.

The cost example below is an author-supplied transfer counterexample, not displayed scene data or a benchmark: a single block-draft pass costs 2.4 illustrative units, each baseline target pass costs one, and verification costs one.
unknowns: No runtime event expectations, bound audiovisual review, measured latency, or learner responses are supplied.

beats.purpose: Distinguish fewer target calls from guaranteed lower latency, including draft work.

narration.text: Drafting still takes time. This is a reduction in target calls, not a guaranteed latency reduction.

transfer_questions.question: If one verification call replaces three target calls, must the total latency be lower even with block drafting?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: No. In the explicit transfer toy, one block-draft pass costs 2.4 units and verification costs one, so speculation takes 3.4 versus 3 baseline units despite all three tokens being accepted.
transfer_questions.justification: One block-draft pass still occupies the critical path before verification: 2.4 plus 1 = 3.4. Parallel proposal positions do not make that pass free. The counterexample is an authored assumption, not a model measurement.

transfer_questions.question: Does the horizontal distance between model boxes represent elapsed inference time?
transfer_questions.expected_answer: Not in this flow diagram. It shows data flow and target-call counts; a latency claim requires an explicitly shared clock and overhead model.
transfer_questions.justification: The scene uses fixed model-box positions and arrows without time-valued intervals. The separate ToyTiming example derives completion from explicit costs, which cannot be recovered from those box distances.
